criteria.criterion: One reserve function in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs sums reader, max_rounds×(planner+critic), producer and verifier from config; Grep shows it called from admission, retry, drain dispatch and the per-round check in run/planning.rs, with no duplicated arithmetic.

Its Admission case is reader + max_rounds×(planner+critic) + producer + verifier. `Athena::preflight` (reading.rs:411) is its only production caller. Grep finds preflight called in first_reading (reading.rs:976, admission and queued re-read), retry (reading.rs:1043), dispatch (run/mod.rs:759 for Dispatch, :927 for Run), and planning.rs:114 (Planner) and :273 (Critic). criteria.criterion: Core test: with a fake driver and the recorded $8.00 budget against the shipped caps (reserve 10.00), admission refuses with a message naming the shortfall and the config line, and the driver records zero invocations. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria.evidence: `admission_refuses_a_job_short_of_the_whole_planning_reserve` passed. It calls `Athena::ask` at job_usd 8.00 with the shipped caps. It asserts a `BudgetShort` error whose text contains "$2.00 short", "$10.00", "[budget] job_usd" and "athena.toml", a counter of 0 invocations, and an unchanged head. A control at 12.00 asserts the reader ran once. I read the base code: its reader-only check (0.50) passes at 8.00, so on base the counter would be 1 and expect_err would fail.

criteria.criterion: Core test: the preflight and the per-round critic check agree at $5.75, at the single-round total and at the full multi-round total; a retry whose recorded spend leaves less than the reserve is refused before planning, and a job with enough budget proceeds. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria.evidence: `round_one_critic_check_follows_the_shared_reserve` passed. It runs the real planning.rs critic check over five rows: (3 rounds, $5.75 left) refused, $3.00 short; (3, 8.74) refused, $0.01 short; (3, 8.75) critic called and landed; (1, 5.74) refused; (1, 5.75) called. On base, the old critic + producer + verifier check (5.75) would call the critic in the first two rows. `every_stage_counts_only_what_is_still_to_run_and_takes_its_caps_from_config` passed: Critic{1} = Admission − reader − planner for max_rounds 1..4. `a_retry_is_judged_on_its_own_spend_and_stopped_before_planning` passed. The funded original job ran 3 planner rounds. The retry is admitted, its reader spends 4.00, and `go` returns BudgetShort ($1.50 short) with no new planner call and an unchanged head. One test named in the plan, `preflight_and_round_checks_agree`, does not exist; the unit table above covers that check.

criteria.criterion: Drain test through the real preflight path: a short job is skipped with its reason on one log line and the next item with enough budget still runs; it fails if the check is removed. Run: cargo test -p athena-cli.
criteria.evidence: `a_short_job_is_skipped_with_its_reason_and_the_next_item_runs` passed. It runs the real `drain::drain` over `RealSteps`. It asserts exactly one `item <A> is left queued:` note, containing "$0.10 short" and "[budget] job_usd" with no newline. findings.summary: Two changed files are outside the expected deliverables list: crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs and crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs.
findings.evidence: run/tests.rs was in the planned files and holds the criterion 4 and 5 tests. tests/drain.rs only gains `held: false` in two `Read` literals, which the new field makes necessary to compile; the CHANGELOG mentions it. Neither edit adds behavior scope.

findings.summary: An existing lifecycle test changed its fake turn cost (0.4 → 0.7) as well as its budget, which goes beyond 'config-only'.
findings.evidence: At 5.60 with cost 0.4, 5.20 would be left, which passes the 5.00 dispatch check, so the cost was raised to keep the test refusing at dispatch. The assertions are unchanged and the test's intent (refused before the next invocation) holds. The plan listed only the job_usd change.

findings.summary: The reserve does not count planner calls from mechanical passes, though each one is still checked before it runs.
findings.evidence: plan_round (planning.rs:41-73) can call the planner up to MAX_MECHANICAL_PASSES extra times per round. budget_reserve counts one planner call per round, as the reading specified, so a job with many mechanical passes can still run short in a later round. Every such call goes through the Planner{round} preflight first, so nothing is spent unchecked. A stricter reserve could add a term for mechanical passes.

findings.summary: In the shipped `mode = "hard"`, the admission reserve counts planning rounds even for readings that will not be planned.
findings.evidence: At admission the reading is not yet known, so ReserveStage::Admission adds max_rounds×(planner+critic) whenever [job_plan] is enabled. The code comments call this deliberate over-reserving, and the request's formula asks for it. With the shipped 12.00 budget it has no effect (0/50 replay).

findings.summary: A test named in the plan does not exist: `preflight_and_round_checks_agree`.
findings.evidence: The planned command for criterion 4(b) would match zero tests. The equivalent check lives in `every_stage_counts_only_what_is_still_to_run_and_takes_its_caps_from_config`, which passed. That test does not include the planned 'Admission Err at 5.75 / Ok at 7.00' cases.

summary: The change does what the retry asked. A single function, `reading::budget_reserve`, adds up reader + max_rounds×(planner+critic) + producer + verifier, reading every cap from athena.toml. `Athena::preflight` applies it at admission, at retry, at dispatch (where the drain reaches it through `go`, and drain.rs now holds a `BudgetShort` item instead of failing it), and before each planner and critic call. No other production code repeats the sum. I ran every new targeted test and all passed: the $8.00 admission refusal with zero invocations, the five-row critic table, the retry stopped before planning, the dispatch hold on a real stored job, the drain skip-and-continue test, and the shipped-budget test. Reading the base code shows each of these would fail there. fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed in Athena's recorded checks. I found no blocker or major problems. The minor ones: two changed files are outside the deliverables list, though they were planned or needed to compile; one existing lifecycle test also changed its fake turn cost, not only its budget; and the reserve does not count planner calls from mechanical passes, though each of those calls is still checked before it runs.
